newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Bangladesh proposes committee to advise U.N. chief.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh proposes committee to advise U.N. chief.

text.p: Bangladesh on Tuesday proposed establishment of a committee to which U.N. secretaries-general could turn for advice.

In a speech to the General Assembly, Foreign Minister Abdus Samad Azad said that while efforts were being made to make the Assembly, the Security Council and other parts of the U.N. system more effective, "we could perhaps also ponder as to how the office of secretary-general could be bolstered."

He proposed creation of a committee "composed in the shape of the general committee of the General Assembly, which the secretary-general could consult, formally or informally, collectively or severally, on important administrative and political issues."
The general, or steering, committee, which organises the Assembly's agenda, has 28 members -- the Assembly president, its 21 vice-presidents and the chairmen of its six main committees.

Such a committee would serve a particularly useful purpose "in ensuring the rightful role of the General Assembly," Azad said, alluding to the diminished authority of that 185-nation body in recent years compared with the enhanced status of the 15-nation Security Council.

In addition to ensuring closer interaction between the secretary-general and the Assembly, the proposed committee would provide the U.N. chief with "the benefit of dispassionate counsel and a feel of the thinking of member states" in an institutional manner, Azad said.
It would also make for "greater transparency in decision-making," he said, referring to openness in diplomacy.

He said the secretary-general was "the most visible symbol and personification" of the United Nations system and "something more than the chief administrative organisation, as stipulated in the U.N. Charter, because he also has important political responsibilities."
